text:
lina: hey - first week and I can view Console staging but trying to call the flags API from my script gives 403. What role do I need?
omar: welcome! you need console.flag.read for viewing and console.flag.write for edits. For scripts prefer a service token with the correct scopes.
lina: how do I get a service token? Okta only showed the staging-app.
omar: DevEx issues short-lived service tokens via the tokens service. File a request with devex-bot or use rwctl auth request if you have CLI. Example: 
```
rwctl auth request --purpose "onboard-script" --scopes "console.flag.read" --ttl 4h
```
devex-bot: created service token request #881 for lina, approvers: devex, infra.
lina: I tried rwctl but it errored: 
```
error: unauthorized: missing:service.token.request
```
omar: that error means your Okta->RBAC mapping doesn't include the service.token.request scope. infra usually syncs that.
infra-oncall: inspecting mappings... found missing claim for group "eng-service-token-users" in staging. Pushing mapping and running sync.
infra-oncall: sync complete. Okta group eng-service-token-users -> RBAC service.token.request added.
lina: retried rwctl request and got a token :tada: can now curl flags with the token.
lina: quick question - if I need to flip a canary in staging via script, what's the approved command?
sylvie: use rwctl to toggle and include actor+reason: 
```
rwctl flags toggle --env staging --flag beta-login --on --actor lina --reason "lina onboarding smoke" --token $TOKEN
```
sylvie: note: prod toggles require runbook + cross-team approval. Don't touch prod without approval.
lina: thanks everyone, adding a short note to the onboarding doc about service tokens, rwctl, and who to ping if mappings fail.
